note: Hearing when the chord changes (hearing-changes:1): a backing track whose chords last one, two or three bars, followed first with the lit chord box and the bass, then with eyes away. The key is moves (any key), named as {{=key}}; the second backing track keeps its distance a 5th up, and a {{?key}} line says what stays the same.

exercise.title: Hear the moment the chord changes
exercise.why: When a chord changes, the bass jumps to the new chord's root, so listening to the lowest note tells you the moment the chord moves.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the backing track in {{=key}}. Each chord lasts one, two or three bars, so counting won't find the changes. Watch the chord boxes, and tap the table each time a new chord box lights.
Listen for the bass jumping to a new note at that moment.

Press Play below to start the backing track again, with the changes in new places. Look away, and tap the table when you hear the chord move. Then look back to check that a new chord box is lit.
If you miss a change, keep your ear on the bass and catch the next one.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the bass still jumps at every change.
